chunks: Muhammad ibn Isma'il from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan from Safwan ibn Yahya from Ibn Muskan from al-Halabi who said:

I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), 'The soft leather shoes are with us in the marketplace, we buy them. So what do you think regarding the prayer in them?' He said, 'Pray in them until it is said to you that they are exactly from the dead (animal) [i.e., their leather is confirmed to be from a dead animal, making them impure].'

key_terms.مَيْتَةٌ: Dead animal (specifically referring to the source of the leather)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on praying in leather shoes of uncertain origin?
ai.summary: This hadith establishes the principle of *al-istishab* (presumption of continuity) in matters of ritual purity, ruling that market-bought leather shoes are presumed pure unless proven otherwise. Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) clarifies that mere uncertainty regarding the animal's slaughter status does not invalidate the prayer, requiring explicit knowledge of the skin being from a *maytah* (dead animal) to render it impure. This ruling facilitates ease for worshippers by preventing excessive doubt (*waswasa*) in daily religious practice.
